text:
sanjay: thinking out loud — we should discuss a capacity-aware degrader/hedge shim for routing. current hedging is blind to reserved capacity and quota windows and is causing noisy preemption.

marta: +1. seen errors where tenants on reserved pools get hedged onto shared which then preempts them back. churn loop.

ev an: can you sketch the desired behavior? is this admission-side or routing-side?

sanjay: idea: split into two pieces — admission filter that enforces hard quota/lease check, then a lightweight hedge-decider that knows pool headroom and soft-sla tiers. admission returns MUST/REJECT/PROVISIONAL, hedge decides parallelism only for PROVISIONAL.

marta: LOVE the split. keeps runtime contract small. how would policy engine expose "headroom"?

sanjay: either as a numeric token count + staleness timestamp, or as a qualitative band (GREEN/YELLOW/RED). numeric is flexible but heavier to keep accurate.

jia: numeric with ttl 500ms might be ok if we accept eventual staleness. but we need graceful fallback if stale — maybe degrade to conservative bands.

ev an: concerns: more chatter across routers to learn headroom. we already push telemetry; this would be another signal. ops cost?

marta: we can piggyback on existing capacity pings. proposal: routers broadcast a small footprint {pool_id, headroom_tokens, seq}. receivers keep last N per pool.

policy-bot: note: policy engine must remain deterministic for canary reproducibility. adding headroom non-determinism could complicate offline sim.

sanjay: good call. so design constraint: policy decisions used by sim must be derivable from recorded signals. store headroom snapshots in sim input.

olivia: edge case: what about tenants who own dedicated capacity but also have burst allowance in shared? we must avoid routing them to shared if they already have active leases.

jia: admission filter should be authoritative: if tenant has active dedicated lease, admission returns MUST_USE_POOL:<pool>, else PROVISIONAL.

ev an: how do we express this in policy DSL? seems like we need a new primitive: lease_status(tenant)->{ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, NONE}.

marta: agree. add a hedge primitive like hedge_band(pool, cost_tier) -> max_parallel. unit tests: simulate lease transitions.

sanjay: rollout plan: 1) add read-only shim in router that computes bands and logs decisions 2) run in shadow for 2 weeks 3) enable admission split with a feature flag 4) canary enable on low-traffic region 5) ramp.

jia: metrics to watch: preemption_count, avg_token_latency, wrong_pool_fallbacks, hedged_parallelism. also sim regression on 99th latency.

olivia: small ask: keep the default conservative — don't increase hedges unless headroom>threshold AND tenant not bursty historically.

e van: where to put the config? runtime or policy repo? ops wants runtime tweakability for emergency changes.

marta: store knobs in runtime flags with policy DSL referencing them as immutable for sim. policy repo defines the mapping from bands->parallelism, runtime flags can nudge thresholds.

sanjay: code sketch for the admission API (very small):

```
AdmissionResult validate(Request r) {
  if (lease_active(r.tenant)) return MUST_USE_POOL(lease_pool);
  if (quota_exhausted(r.tenant)) return REJECT;
  return PROVISIONAL;
}
```

and hedge decision pseudocode:
```
if (admission == PROVISIONAL) {
  band = headroom_to_band(pool.headroom);
  max_parallel = policy.hedge_table[band][r.cost_tier];
}
```

policy-bot: reminder: update policy-evals to include synthetic headroom sequences for regression tests.

jia: agree. I'll add a small harness that replays headroom signals and asserts no >5% increase in preemptions.

olivia: one more: ensure observability includes the snapshot that led to the decision so we can debug postmortems. attach pool_seq to request trace.

sanjay: good. last question: can we avoid cross-region blasts? headroom should be region-scoped; only global tenants might be allowed cross-region hedging under opt-in.

marta: keep region isolation default. GLOBAL_HEDGE opt-in flag for enterprise tenants.

e van: sounds actionable. I'll open an RFC PR describing interface shapes and a small compatibility shim for older routers.

sanjay: thanks all. we'll sync in arch sync next Tues. quick follow-ups: @marta can you list the policy primitives you'll add? @jia can you start the sim harness?

marta: will do.

jia: on it.
